Heard Sri Akhilesh Kalra, learned counsel for the petitioners, learned Standing Counsel appearing for the State-opposite parties no.1 and 4, Sri R.K. Chaudhary, learned counsel appearing for opposite party no.2, Sri Avinash Singh Vishen, learned counsel appearing for opposite parties no.3 and 6 and Sri Naresh Chandra Mehrotra, learned counsel appearing for opposite party no.5.
2.

This writ petition has been filed with the following main prayers:-
"(i) Issue a writ, order or direction in the nature of Certiorari quashing the requisition orders dated 30.04.2024 passed by respondent no.4, District Magistrate, Pratapgarh Hira Lal And Others vs State Of U.P. sentences.text: 1 (Annexure No.1).

(ii) issue an appropriate writ, order or direction in the nature of mandamus restricting the respondents from disturbing the possession of the petitioners during the 2024 Lok Sabha Elections and for all future elections.

(iii) Issue an appropriate writ, order or direction in the nature of mandamus commanding the opposite parties to use the area of the Mahuli Mandi premises that is lying vacant instead of disturbing the possession of the petitioners.

(iv) Issue an appropriate writ, order or direction in the nature of Mandamus commanding the opposite parties to give proportionate and adequate compensation to the petitioners in the even the Mandi premises are requisitioned."
3. It is the case of the petitioners that they are license holders and allottees of various shops at Mahuli Mandi, Pratapgarh and have been in continuous possession of the area allotted to them and have raised necessary and temporary infrastructure for the purpose of utilizing the allotted premises for selling vegetables and fruits.

The opposite parties intend to create store rooms for storing EVMs and VVPAT machines for the general elections scheduled to be held on 20th and 25th May, 2024 and have issued necessary orders under Section 160 of the Representation of the People Act, 1951 for acquisition of the premises of Mahuli Mandi, Pratapgarh.
The petitioners personally and through their Vendors Society sent several representations to the opposite parties as they anticipated that such requisition order to be passed in January, 2024 itself.
Opposite party no.6 rejected the representations filed by the petitioners on 12.02.2024.
The petitioners are being prevented from earning their livelihood, which is part of their right to live by the order of the requisition.
4. In several litigations relating to other Mandi areas in neighbouring districts, the Election Commission has refrained from acquiring such Mandis.
The petitioners, however, have not been heard and their representations have been rejected and the requisition order has been passed on 30.04.2024.

5. Learned counsel appearing for the Election Commission of India has pointed out the order passed in Public Interest Litigation (PIL) No.385 of 2024, Kashi Prasad Yadav Vs. State of U.P. and others by a Division Bench of this Court on 02.05.2024, wherein in a matter relating to the same Mandi at Pratapgarh, the Court has refused to interfere and finding is recorded that the petition filed as a Public Interest Litigation was in fact a proxy petition on behalf of the shop keepers, arathiyas and labourers.
6.

sentences.text: It has been submitted that the license holders have now come directly before this Court.

It has also been pointed out that under Article 329 of the Constitution of India, the Court would ordinarily not interfere in any sort of litigation, which might to hamper the conduct of elections by the Election Commission.

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the petitioners has stated that a large area is lying vacant adjacent to the Mahuli Mandi, Pratapgarh.
8. This Court sitting in Writ jurisdiction, is not competent to decide which land should be requisitioned by the Election Commission in place of Mahuli Mandi, Pratapgarh.

9. Learned counsel for the Election Commission of India, on the basis of instructions, says that the premise of Mahuli Mandi, Pratapgarh is secure and it has pacca shed over it and it is more secure for the purposes of storing EVMs and VVPAT machines.

10. This Court is of the opinion that in case the petitioners' livelihood is being effected in any manner due to temporary requisition for the election purposes by the Election Commission of India,
the petitioners may file their objections under Section 161 of the Representation of the People Act,
1951 for grant of appropriate compensation after the elections are over.

11. With the aforesaid observation and direction, the writ petition stands disposed of.
.

(Brij Raj Singh, J.) (Sangeeta Chandra, J.) Order Date :- 15.5.2024 Rao/-
